title: What is four sevenths plus six sevenths?
description: Four sevenths and six sevenths are drawn on strips cut into seven equal parts. The units are counted to give ten sevenths, and seven sevenths make one whole. Keeko doubts the answer by adding the tops and adding the bottoms.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the number of units, and when there are more than seven sevenths, one whole comes out. Watch for the slip of adding the bottom numbers too.

video_script.why: A learner adds fractions with the same fractional unit, and sees that more than seven sevenths means more than one whole.
video_script.substitution: the book's own sum four sevenths plus six sevenths on rectangular strips
video_script.anchor: two rectangular strips, each cut into seven equal parts
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the tops and adds the bottoms and gets ten fourteenths. Ten fourteenths is five sevenths, which is less than six sevenths alone, so the idea is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: ten sevenths, which is one and three sevenths

final_answer.spoken: four sevenths and six sevenths make ten sevenths, which is one and three sevenths

video_script.fraction_reading: four sevenths, six sevenths, seven sevenths, ten sevenths, three sevenths, ten fourteenths, five sevenths
never_show: ten fourteenths written as the sum before Keeko's doubt
maths_rules: both fractions have the same fractional unit 1/7
add the number of units: 4 + 6 = 10, so 4/7 + 6/7 = 10/7
slip: Keeko adds the tops and the bottoms and gets 10/14 = 5/7, which is less than 6/7
video_script.design: Two strips cut into sevenths stay on the board. The ten shaded parts are counted, and the first seven fill one whole strip.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two strips cut into 7 equal parts, 4 parts shaded on the first in teal and 6 parts shaded on the second in amber; the words sum? appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.strips: two strips cut into seven equal parts appear, with four parts shaded in teal on the first and six parts shaded in amber on the second

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it asks for the sum of two fractions.
<bookmark mark='strips'/>One strip shows four sevenths, and the other strip shows six sevenths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is four sevenths plus six sevenths?

beats.on_screen: the two strips hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: one strip of 7 equal parts, each part labelled 1/7, fully shaded and labelled 1 whole; the bottom number 7 is circled

marks.unit: a strip splits into seven equal parts, each labelled 1/7, and the bottom number is circled
marks.whole: all seven parts are shaded and the strip is labelled one whole

narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>Both strips are cut into seven equal parts, so every part is one seventh. This is the fractional unit.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>When all seven parts are shaded, the strip is one whole.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the two fractions are four sevenths and six sevenths.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sum of 4/7 and 6/7
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the sum of the two fractions.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the same fractional unit 1/7; 4/7 is 4 units and 6/7 is 6 units

marks.same: both strips carry the label unit 1/7
marks.units: 4/7 is marked as 4 units and 6/7 as 6 units

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step one, both fractions have the same fractional unit, one seventh.
<bookmark mark='units'/>Four sevenths is four units, and six sevenths is six units.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: add the number of units: 4 + 6 = 10 units of 1/7, that is 10/7

marks.join: the shaded parts of both strips slide together into a row

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step two, slide the shaded parts of the two strips into one row.
<bookmark mark='total'/>Four plus six is ten, so we have ten units of one seventh. That is ten sevenths.

marks.whole: the first seven shaded parts fill one whole strip
marks.rest: 3 more parts are left over and 10/7 = 7/7 + 3/7 = 1 + 3/7 is written

beats.colours: the whole strip = teal, the 3 extra parts = amber
narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>Step three, seven sevenths make one whole. The first seven parts fill one strip.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Three more parts are left over, so ten sevenths is one whole and three sevenths.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Four sevenths and six sevenths make ten sevenths, which is one and three sevenths.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two strips
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says add the tops and add the bottoms: 10/14; a strip of 14 equal blocks with 10 shaded sits beside 6/7 and is shorter; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.short: a strip of fourteen equal blocks with ten shaded sits beside six sevenths and is shorter
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and the unit 1/7 stays on the strips

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks it is ten fourteenths, because four plus six is ten and seven plus seven is fourteen.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Ten fourteenths is only five sevenths, which is less than the six sevenths we started with.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A sum cannot be smaller than one of its parts. The pieces stay sevenths, and we only count them.
